whatIs: Astryx is Meta's open source design system: React components built with StyleX, tokens for color, typography, spacing and motion, swappable themes and full-page templates. Besides the basic pieces, it includes components for chat interfaces, command palettes and app shells.

Its CLI generates, inside your project, the documentation that coding agents read, so it's a good choice if you build the interface with Claude Code, Cursor or v0 and want them to follow the same conventions on every screen.
uses: Setting up a React app with a complete theme from the start, without defining colors and spacing by hand.
Building an assistant interface with the chat components: message list, composer and tool calls.
Running npx @astryxdesign/cli init so the coding agent uses the system's components and tokens.
caveats: It's in beta, so the components' API may still change between versions.
It requires React 19 or later and uses StyleX for styling; in a project with Tailwind you end up with two styling systems side by side.
It's a complete design system: adopting it halfway in an app that already has its own interface pays off little.
pricingNote: Open source under the MIT license; there's no paid plan.
idealFor: Teams starting a React app who want a design system ready to work with agents.
